items.title: Tibet earthquake, Gulf attacks and Ukraine talks: world news, October 23, 2026 | One Turn
items.excerpt: # Tibet earthquake, Gulf attacks and Ukraine talks A magnitude 7.0 earthquake in Tibet killed at least 16 people, while attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia pushed Brent crude to a five-month high. Russia said it would resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine as strikes continued on both sides. Finland licensed the world's first deep geological repository for spent nuclear fuel, and Pope Leo's doctors said he needs no further cancer treatment. ## The day's stories ... ### Iran says seven tankers hit or damaged in Strait of Hormuz Iran said seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged overnight into Thursday in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they hit four vessels in the northern Gulf and that three more struck naval mines near the strait. Seafarers told Euronews that traffic through the waterway has fallen 90% since the war began and that at least 95 commercial seafarers have died. ... ### US and Israel reported to be planning new strikes on Iran A person briefed on war planning told NPR the US and Israel are preparing for a possible attack on Iran in early November, after the US midterm elections. President Trump told reporters the US had "knocked the hell out of them" and "may do it a little bit further." US Central Command said its naval blockade of Iran has stopped all seaborne trade except approved humanitarian aid for 100 days, and Iran said it is prepared. ... ### Brent crude tops $113, highest since May Brent crude rose above $113 a barrel, its highest level since May, after attacks in Saudi Arabia, tanker hits near Hormuz and Trump's remarks on possible new strikes on Iran. Brent stood at $113.62 in the latest data, up 6.6% over the month. Citi said it sees more upside risk to prices, while rising Chinese imports suggest China is drawing less from its stockpiles. ... ### Putin agrees to resume talks as strikes on Kyiv continue Vladimir Putin said Russia is ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, aimed at a final agreement rather than a pause in fighting, after meeting US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg. Hours later Russian missiles struck Kyiv, and Ukrainian authorities reported at least nine people killed across the country in 24 hours, while Moscow said it downed hundreds of Ukrainian drones. Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks showed "no real change" in Russia's attitude. Why it matters: The resumption of three-way talks is the latest US attempt to end Europe's largest war, though fighting has not eased. ... ### France restricts protests and extends Paris curfew after riots ... President Emmanuel Macron said only union-organized protests will be allowed after weekend riots, and Lyon and Marseille banned all protests on Saturday. Paris extended an 11 pm to 6 am curfew in some areas until Monday, top museums will close Saturday, and police numbers will rise 20%; a court lifted a Paris ban for Thursday's student march, which drew thousands. Macron blamed "ultra-left groups," and France's 10-year bond yield hit a 24-year high. ... ### Study estimates heat killed 50,000 in European cities this summer New research estimates that heat killed a record 50,000 people in European cities between June and August, with scientists attributing two in three of those deaths to climate change. Death rates were highest in Malta, Italy and Hungary, and researchers said poor health, loneliness and poverty worsened the toll. ... ### IUCN classifies 96% of assessed coral reefs as critically endangered In its first global assessment of coral reef ecosystems, the IUCN classified 96% of assessed shallow-water reef systems as critically endangered. It warned nearly all reefs risk collapse within 50 years. ... ### Polls show tie before Brazil's Lula-Bolsonaro runoff Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday ... ### US tech stocks fall on AI spending concerns The Nasdaq fell 2.6% as investors questioned heavy spending on artificial intelligence, and the S&P 500 closed down 1.21%. Meta shares sank nearly 7% after AI spending pushed its free cash flow negative, and its credit default swap prices reached record highs; CoreWeave shares are down 36% in October. Nvidia's Jensen Huang said demand for neocloud firms is strong but capital is scarce. ... ### AI-found PHP flaws force websites offline worldwide Governments and companies took websites offline after PHP's developers disclosed two critical vulnerabilities, found by AI, that let attackers run code on servers without logging in. Fixes were released Wednesday, but a major tech firm reported millions of exploitation attempts and Amazon said it saw attacks before the warning went public. A UK minister said 500 new vulnerabilities had been found in government systems. ... ## Oil climbs as stocks fall on AI worries ... Brent crude rose to $113.62, up 0.4% on the day and 6.6% over the month, after tanker attacks near Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and reports of planned US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Stocks fell on concerns over AI spending, with the S&P 500 down 1.21%, the Euro Stoxx 50 down 1.94% as French bond yields hit a 24-year high, and the Nikkei down 0.93%. The US 10-year yield dropped 3.75% to 4.953% as investors moved toward bonds, while gold slipped 0.95% to $4,021.90. Natural gas fell 2.5% and is down 17.3% over the month. ### Gulf conflict lifts oil Attacks on tankers in Hormuz and on Saudi oil and aviation sites, plus reports of new US-Israeli strike plans on Iran, pushed Brent to its highest since May. Higher fuel costs are feeding protests and weaker sentiment in Europe. ... UK consumer confidence fell at its fastest rate since 2016, and Canada announced support for manufacturers hit by US tariffs while opening trade talks with Turkey. Japan's core inflation reached 2.1%, the highest this year.

items.title: Early Edition: October 23, 2026
items.excerpt: RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR ... Russian President Vladimir Putin yesterday said that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe. Putin said the peace should be in its “final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time.” Vladimir Soldatkin reports for Reuters. Trump on Wednesday called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine, U.S. officials told the Wall Street Journal. The sources said the system was working more normally yesterday shortly after their conversation. Trump told Musk he was frustrated the system’s speeds remained capped. Trump yesterday said Musk had restored Ukraine’s Starlink access but declined to comment when asked about if he had spoken to Musk about the matter. Alexander Ward and Lara Seligman report; Jacob Bogage and Kanishka Singh report for Reuters. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov today told reporters that reports that U.S. citizen Stephen James Hubbard was released in exchange for the recent release of Russian war blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk from custody in Montenegro were false. Dmitry Antonov reports for Reuters. A tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is heading towards New York, ship-tracking data viewed by Reuters showed today. The tanker is the first to be transferred to the United States after Trump announced a deal to import Russian diesel. ISRAEL-HAMAS WAR ... Israeli strikes and gunfire in Gaza yesterday killed at least four people, according to local health officials. In Gaza City, a strike on a car killed at least one person, another strike killed a Palestinian man on a bike in the southern city of Khan Younis, and a strike killed a man near Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza. Gunfire killed a woman near the northern Jabalia refugee camp. The Israeli military said it had struck Hamas militants in Gaza City, Khan Younis, and Nuseirat, but that it was not aware of the reported incident in Jabalia. Nidal al-Mughrabi reports for Reuters. WEST BANK DEVELOPMENTS ... The Israeli military today said they prevented a “terror attack against Israeli civilians” in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron when they shot and killed two men. The IDF said the two men were carrying guns. The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later instructed security forces to cordon off Hebron and prepare to fully close all of the West Bank. Shlomo Mor and Sam Mednick report for AP News. ... A pair of studies published today in the Nature Health journal say severe heat killed more than 50,000 people in European cities and towns this summer. Researchers said that the figure is three times as many people as would have died had manmade global warming not occurred. The studies are based on a combination of factors that influence heat-related health risks in particular locations, and the estimates are not based on official death reports. Raymond Zhang reports for the New York Times. The International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Ecosystems yesterday announced that almost all of the world’s shallow-water coral reefs have now been classified as critically endangered. It was the group’s first global assessment of shallow-water reef ecosystems, and it said heat stress because of climate change is the overwhelming reason for the finding. Catrin Einhorn reports for the New York Times. OTHER GLOBAL DEVELOPMENTS

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield drops back to 5% this week as investors seek cover from AI worries
items.excerpt: Investors ran for cover this week as artificial intelligence fears hit stocks, driving the 10-year Treasury below 5%. The benchmark yield stayed below 5% on Friday, after falling beneath that level Thursday for the first time in a month, as investors continued to express misgivings over the massive debt being taken on by technology companies to finance their build out of AI networks. Tech stocks sank, bond yields on outstanding tech debt rose and spreads on credit default swaps widened in a host of AI companies. "The selloff in tech stocks drove the flight-to-quality bid, compounded by continued weakness in the French sovereign market," BMO's credit strategy team said in a note Friday. "Interestingly, the focus on weakness in the equity market ... [has] overshadowed the move in the energy market, with Treasuries rallying despite WTI crude oil testing $100/bbl." On Friday, yields on 10-year U.S. Treasurys Add To Watchlist — used to price mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — rose by 1 basis point to 4.966%. The yield on the 2-year Treasury Add To Watchlist note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve policy, increased by 2 basis points to 4.658%. Yields on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys Add To Watchlist — which react to geopolitical developments — were relatively flat at 5.292%. ... The bounce back in Treasury prices ... Next week, the focus will turn to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, due on Wednesday. The market doesn't expect the central bank to raise rates this month, but is pricing in a roughly 72% probability of a quarter percentage point hike in December, according to the CME Group FedWatch tool. ... "At this stage, the tightening of financial conditions hasn't been dramatic enough to preclude another rate hike this year, although a sustained deterioration could readily alter the Fed's policy calculus," BMO Capital said. ... Traders are awaiting Friday's flash S&P Global PMI readings on manufacturing and services for a fresh view on U.S. growth and inflation. Meanwhile, rising energy costs continue to weigh on the inflation outlook. West Texas Intermediate futures Add To Watchlist for December delivery climbed another 1.6% to $101.10 a barrel on Friday, while Brent crude Add To Watchlist, the international oil benchmark, traded 1.4% higher, at $114.71 a barrel. Firmer energy prices come as fresh attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabian oil installations drove new fears over an oil supply squeeze. Reports earlier this week suggested that the U.S. and Israel could resume strikes against Iran following the midterm elections on Nov. 3.

items.excerpt: Heavier fighting in Iran could resume in the coming weeks as military reinforcements arrive and some U.S. personnel leave the region. This shift comes as a person briefed on the U.S. and Israel's war planning told NPR that the countries were preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran after the U.S. midterms. Iran said it is prepared. Traffic in ... - 🎧 There are clear signs of preparations for a possible attack, NPR's Greg Myre tells Up First. The U.S. is deploying a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth recently visited Israel to meet with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. President Trump will likely consider military action after Nov. 3 to avoid a spike in oil prices before the midterm elections. In response, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Iran is ready for both diplomacy and war. While the U.S. and Israel possess the power to inflict heavy damage, Iran shows no signs of making significant concessions, Myre says. Instead, it demands formal control over the Strait of Hormuz and the withdrawal of U.S. troops from the region. Although Election Day is more than a week away, almost 21 million Americans have already voted, either by mail or early in-person voting, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab. - 🎧 That number of votes so far is a lot and is an increase of about 2 million since yesterday, according to NPR's Saige Miller. In key battleground states, early voting is significantly higher compared to the last midterm election. While the early voting data should not be overinterpreted as a predictor of final results, it shows Democrats voting at higher rates than Republicans, Miller says. Unaffiliated voters are also participating early. Democrats are generally more likely to vote early, and Republicans are more likely to turn out on Election Day, Miller says. - ➡️ A federal judge in California is limiting the Department of Homeland Security's pre-election field operations. The agency says they aim to identify noncitizens who allegedly voted illegally in nine states. - ➡️ The NPR App has all of NPR's election coverage in one place — from the biggest stories across the country, to the issues that matter close to home. items.excerpt: The beloved children's musician Raffi continues to charm audiences with his timeless songs. Fifty years after his debut children's album, his music remains a staple for young children. Raffi's latest album, “Love is Everywhere,” comes out Friday. It features songs celebrating everything from individuality to the importance of voting. He believes that while technology changes, the essence of childhood remains the same. In an interview with The Associated Press, Raffi emphasized the importance of protecting children's development from excessive technology. He also discussed his commitment to not exploiting children through advertising and how it caused him to turn down a movie offer for “Baby Beluga.” NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Country Music Hall of Famer John Anderson has died at age 71. His family announced his death Wednesday on his social media accounts. Anderson was known for his high, yearning vocal style and hits such as “Swingin’,” “Wild and Blue,” and “Black Sheep.” Born in Apopka, Florida, he moved to Nashville, Tennessee, after high school. He worked odd jobs before his commercial breakthrough in 1977. Anderson was a “New Traditionalist,” sometimes compared to George Jones and Merle Haggard. He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024 and won two Country Music Association awards. ... LOS ANGELES (AP) — Jay-Z once called John Legend “our voice,” but Pharrell Williams had a different idea for Legend's baritone. On his new album, “Muse,” Legend dials back his powerhouse vocals, opting for a more conversational delivery at Williams’ urging. The album, out Friday, marks Legend’s first full collaboration with Williams after more than 20 years of friendship. Recorded mostly at Williams’ studio in Paris, it grew from Legend’s appearance on Clipse’s “The Birds Don’t Sing.” In an interview, Legend discussed Williams’ influence, Jay-Z’s compliment and composing his first original stage score for a new musical.
